candidates.support: Direct written-form control, explicit Greek negative wording and its dependent Latin; making-verb ellipsis supports the current natural English
candidates.countercase: Belonging fits the adjacent his people/flock parallel and is present within Hebrew qere and the Hebrew-based Latin control; following the written form alone proves no chronological priority

candidates.english: He made us, and we are his
candidates.support: Direct reading-tradition control, Hebrew-based Latin selected text and possessive poetic context
candidates.countercase: Possessive context could motivate normalization; older Greek negative tradition must be explained rather than ignored. Neither direction of a copying change is observed

chronology: Translation/work dates, edition dates and physical-copy dates must remain separate. This pass lacks a dated direct Hebrew manuscript collation and complete hand/version apparatus; antiquity of Greek as a translation does not date every selected reading. No automatic oldest-wins choice is warranted; removing age preference leaves the same provisional retention.
english_assessment: Both clauses give natural but different meanings. Current negative rendering supplies the ellipted making verb/object, not a lost Hebrew phrase. Belonging reinforces possession already explicit in his people/flock; it is not evidence for a new theology. No blind whole-verse comparison or corpus-wide superiority measure.
